fulltext: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，据日经亚洲 11 月 25 日报道，三星电子和 SK 海力士两大存储企业，正在采用由长江存储率先开发的芯片堆叠技术。
这一举措表明，长江存储已经迅速赶上那些规模更大的半导体竞争对手，并拥有了庞大的知识产权储备。
三位知情人士透露，三星和 SK 海力士一直在探索 3D NAND 闪存的堆叠技术，并通过交叉许可协议，同意采用长江存储 Xtacking 中的部分相关技术。
IT之家查询公开资料获悉，晶栈 Xtacking 是长江存储核心技术品牌，始于 2018 年，可实现在两片独立的晶圆上加工外围电路和存储单元，这样有利于选择更先进的逻辑工艺，从而让 NAND 获取更高的 I/O 接口速度及更多的操作功能。
在传统 3DNAND 架构中，外围电路约占芯片面积 20~30%，晶栈 Xtacking 技术创新的将外围电路置于存储单元之上，从而实现比传统 3D NAND 更高的存储密度，芯片面积可减少约 25%。
晶栈 Xtacking 技术充分利用存储单元和外围电路的独立加工优势，实现了并行的、模块化的产品设计及制造，产品开发时间可缩短三个月，生产周期可缩短 20%。此外，这种模块化的方式也为引入 NAND 外围电路的创新功能以实现 NAND 闪存的定制化提供了可能。

fulltext: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，智界汽车今日宣布迎来第 20 万台整车下线。三年沉淀，智界逐步完成从一款车到覆盖轿车、SUV、MPV 多个产品品类的拓展。
官方称，智界 V9 斩获 26 年 40 万元以上 MPV 累计销量第一；智界 RX 刷新浙赛中国品牌量产 SUV 最快圈速，以“为驾驶而生”为底，做鸿蒙智行最好开的车；智界 R7 已累计收获超 13 万车主的选择。
IT之家注：智界汽车（LUXEED）是由华为与奇瑞汽车合作推出的高端智能汽车品牌，属鸿蒙智行体系，融合华为智能技术与奇瑞整车制造优势，产品搭载 HarmonyOS 鸿蒙座舱及华为 ADS 智驾系统等。另外，奇瑞去年 8 月与华为在深圳进行了智界品牌战略 2.0 合作协议签约，正式宣布品牌进入 2.0 阶段。
今年 10 月，工信部《道路机动车辆生产企业及产品公告》（第 412 批）显示，安徽智界新能源汽车有限公司被列入“拟发布新准入车辆生产企业”清单，也就是将获批独立造车资质。奇瑞汽车股份有限公司执行副总裁戚士龙回应智界独立造车时表示，希望智界团队更像新势力企业，而不是简单做成“大一号”的传统车企。

cards.title: Gemini for Home gets faster responses, smoother chats, and fixes for follow-up and music bugs
cards.title_cn: Gemini for Home 获得更快的响应、更流畅的聊天以及修复后续和音乐错误
cards.summary: 【Google】TL;DR Google has fully rolled out speed improvements for common Gemini for Home smart home commands. The latest update fixes bugs affecting follow-up commands and stopping media playback. Google is al…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

The story of Gemini for Home’s transition from Google Assistant is beginning to take a more positive turn. We’ve seen some users warming up to Google’s new voice assistant, particularly after noticeable improvements in response times. Now, Google is giving Gemini more polish, whether you’re asking it to switch off the lights or tell your kids a bedtime story.

With its second November update, Google has confirmed that speed improvements for common smart home commands have fully rolled out to Gemini for Home Early Access users. So, whether you’re turning on the lights or adjusting the thermostat, Gemini should respond and act faster.

Google has also fixed a bug where Gemini would occasionally forget the context of a conversation. For example, asking Gemini to turn the living room lights back on shortly after telling it to turn them off should now work as expected. Another fix addresses an issue where Gemini would incorrectly insist that nothing was playing when asked to stop music or other media.

Beyond these fixes, Google is beginning to roll out the upgraded Gemini Live experience it announced last week alongside energy-saving improvements for Nest thermostats and new features for Google Home cameras. Over the coming weeks, Google Home Premium subscribers will get faster, more natural conversations with Gemini, along with the ability to set timers, add reminders, and control smart home devices without ending an ongoing chat.

Gemini is also becoming a better storyteller. Starting today, stories will feature more expressive voices and varied pacing, and you can steer the plot as Gemini narrates. And if you own a supported smart display, you’ll be able to tap a new “Sources” option to see the websites Gemini used to answer your questions.

With Google Assistant set to retire from smart home devices in August 2027, every little improvement counts. And while more entertaining bedtime stories are a welcome addition, getting Gemini to remember which lights you were talking about is likely to make a bigger difference in everyday life.

2026 年 11 月 25 日 — 下午 3:15（美国东部时间）
Gemini for Home 从 Google Assistant 过渡的故事开始出现更积极的转变。我们已经看到一些用户对谷歌的新语音助手产生了兴趣，特别是在响应时间显着改善之后。现在，谷歌正在对 Gemini 进行更多改进，无论你是要求它关灯还是给你的孩子讲睡前故事。
在 11 月的第二次更新中，Google 确认常见智能家居命令的速度改进已全面推广到 Gemini，供家庭抢先体验用户使用。所以，无论你是开灯还是调节恒温器，双子座都应该更快地做出反应和行动。
谷歌还修复了双子座偶尔会忘记对话上下文的错误。例如，在告诉 Gemini 关闭客厅灯后不久，要求 Gemini 将其重新打开，现在应该可以按预期工作。另一个修复解决了双子座在被要求停止音乐或其他媒体时错误地坚持没有播放任何内容的问题。
除了这些修复之外，谷歌还开始推出上周宣布的升级版 Gemini Live 体验，以及 Nest 恒温器的节能改进和 Google Home 摄像头的新功能。在接下来的几周内，Google Home Premium 订阅者将能够与 Gemini 进行更快、更自然的对话，并且能够设置计时器、添加提醒和控制智能家居设备，而无需结束正在进行的聊天。
双子座也正在成为一个更好的讲故事的人。从今天开始，故事将采用更具表现力的声音和不同的节奏，你可以按照双子座的叙述来引导情节。如果您拥有受支持的智能显示器，您将能够点击新的“来源”选项来查看 Gemini 用于回答您的问题的网站。
随着 Google Assistant 将于 2027 年 8 月从智能家居设备中退出，每一个微小的改进都至关重要。虽然更多有趣的睡前故事是受欢迎的补充，但让双子座记住你正在谈论的灯光可能会给日常生活带来更大的变化。

cards.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
cards.title_cn: Anthropic 的 Dario Amodei 称将人类控制权交给人工智能的指控“荒谬”
cards.summary: 【Anthropic】Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushes back against rivals’ accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI, even as leading AI companies increasingly automate their own research and model devel…

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.”

“We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.”

The statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.”
Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.”

“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.”

But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power.

Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software.

Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.”

Still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. The company said in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic’s codebase. An independent assessment published this month by AI safety research nonprofit METR found that Anthropic’s models are improving at about twice their historical rate, primarily driven by AI-assisted research.
In its own IPO filings, Anthropic describes how each successive generation of Claude accelerates the development of the next, a process it refers to as “closing the loop.”

“As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding,” Amodei wrote.

The problem with “meaningful human supervision or understanding” is that AI is already advancing faster than engineers and safety experts can fully audit it, leaving them increasingly reliant on other AI systems to act as judge and jury. The issue compounds when AI models engage in deceptive behavior, particularly when they recognize they’re being evaluated, making them harder to trust and control.

Still, Anthropic is by no means the only company that is pursuing RSI or building AI systems to automate more and more human tasks. This week, OpenAI claimed to have solved one of the biggest open problems in computer science — the exact speed limit of matrix multiplication, which is the mathematical engine behind modern computing, including deep learning and physics simulations.

In his post, Amodei accused competitors of engaging in a “vibes-based commercial and political positioning,” disingenuously throwing around phrases like “human control and agency” or “AI should just be a tool” without approaching the AI race any differently.

“Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation,” Amodei wrote. “Every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards.”

Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 反驳了 Anthropic 认为我们应该“让人类自由意志”屈服于人工智能系统的说法。在周三的一篇长篇 X 帖子中，阿莫迪称这个建议“荒谬”。
“我们永远不应该为了效率或安全而牺牲合法性或自决权，”他写道。这种反对专制的论点逐字逐句地反对人工智能的治理，我同样强烈地感到，将治理交给人工智能是一个坏主意……没有人仔细阅读过我的文章或我的采访，可以合理地得出我相信任何不同的东西的结论。
在发表这一声明之前，Anthropic 的竞争对手越来越多地异口同声地表示，如果人工智能的开发不负责任，人类的能动性可能会面临风险。本月早些时候，OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 表示，他希望确保人们继续拥有“未来的代理权”。
Meta 的首席人工智能官 Alexandr Wang 也在 X 的一篇文章中写道，我们“不应该同意将社会‘移交给’人工智能”。
“很难想象一个人类能够保持对完全不受约束的递归自我完善的控制的世界，”王写道。 “既然我们已经到了能力进步的科学和技术问题可能得到解决的地步，我们不仅必须在安全、协调和安保等极其紧迫的领域取得进展，而且必须开始深思熟虑地思考如何取得进展。”
但阿莫迪在发表的文章中声称，他多次主张对人工智能进行民主监督，称该技术应该加强民主制度，而人类应该保留最终决策权。
阿莫迪指出，广泛放弃人类自由意志与“随着人工智能系统的进步，它们能够以更自动化的方式完成特定任务”的想法之间存在差异。作为例子，他举了人工智能驾驶汽车、设计抗癌药物或编写端到端软件的例子。
阿莫迪建议，不要采用递归自我改进（RSI），即无需人类帮助即可自我改进的人工智能。许多安全专家认为 RSI 不可避免地会导致人类失去控制，阿莫迪含蓄地承认了这一点，并写道，“我们可能希望限制这一过程。”
尽管如此，Anthropic 仍在通过将人工智能纳入其自身研发中越来越多的份额，为 RSI 奠定基础。该公司 6 月份表示，Claude 编写了超过 80% 的代码，这些代码已合并到 Anthropic 的代码库中。人工智能安全研究非营利组织 METR 本月发布的一份独立评估发现，Anthropic 的模型正在以历史速度的两倍左右改进，这主要是由人工智能辅助研究推动的。
在其自己的 IPO 文件中，Anthropic 描述了每一代 Claude 如何加速下一代的开发，这个过程被称为“闭环”。
阿莫迪写道：“正如我们在 11 月初公开表示的那样，我们认为克劳德在没有有意义的人类监督或理解的情况下完全自主地建立连续的前沿模型是不安全的。”
“有意义的人类监督或理解”的问题在于，人工智能的发展速度已经超出了工程师和安全专家对其进行全面审核的速度，这使得他们越来越依赖其他人工智能系统来充当法官和陪审团。当人工智能模型出现欺骗行为时，尤其是当它们意识到自己正在接受评估时，问题就会变得更加复杂，这使得它们更难信任和控制。
尽管如此，Anthropic 绝不是唯一一家追求 RSI 或构建人工智能系统以自动化越来越多的人工任务的公司。本周，OpenAI 声称已经解决了计算机科学中最大的开放问题之一——矩阵乘法的精确速度限制，矩阵乘法是现代计算（包括深度学习和物理模拟）背后的数学引擎。
阿莫迪在帖子中指责竞争对手从事“基于氛围的商业和政治定位”，不诚实地抛出“人类控制和代理”或“人工智能应该只是一种工具”等短语，而没有以任何不同的方式对待人工智能竞赛。
“当然，他们提供的产品在任务自动化方面没有重大差异；每家公司似乎都在发布越来越有能力实现任务自动化的模型，”阿莫迪写道。 “每家公司都声称了解这种自动化的风险和缺点，并提供保障措施。”

cards.title_cn: [视频][银河之声]来认识一下来自墨西哥的医生，他的银河手表帮助他照顾他的母亲和他自己
cards.summary: 【Samsung】For emergency physician Dr. José Elías Ortega, 37, his smartwatch was once simply used for counting steps, managing notifications, and keeping time. But a few years ago, his Galaxy Watch helped him ma…
fulltext: Samsung Newsroom
on November 25, 2026

Voices of Galaxy is a series of real stories spotlighting Samsung Galaxy users who use their passion, creativity, and determination along with technology to make a positive impact on their own lives, communities, and the world around them.
For emergency physician Dr. José Elías Ortega, 37, his smartwatch was once simply used for counting steps, managing notifications, and keeping time.
But a few years ago, his Galaxy Watch helped him make a critical decision while he was visiting his mother, who lives alone.

One morning after a night shift at the hospital, Dr. José Elías Ortega found his mother on the floor, trying to get up but unable to focus her gaze or respond to him. Drawing on his medical training, he suspected a stroke. Then he thought of his Galaxy Watch and quickly put it on her wrist to check her vital signs.

The watch detected her oxygen saturation was below normal, changing Dr. José Elías Ortega’s initial assessment. He gave her oxygen and took her to the hospital, where the medical team diagnosed her with influenza-related pneumonia. Fortunately, his mother stabilized and was later discharged.
“If I hadn’t had the watch on hand… we wouldn’t have realized her problem was respiratory,” said Dr. José Elías Ortega.

His mother’s rescue was just the beginning of how Galaxy Watch changed his life story. It has also supported Dr. José Elías Ortega through his own journey with thyroid cancer, helping him improve his sleeping and activity habits.

For Dr. José Elías Ortega, both experiences show the value of detecting health signals many can easily miss. Rather than replacing professional medical treatment, such data from wearables informs users of potential health issues so they can seek care sooner.
Learn more about Dr. José Elías Ortega’s story in the video below.

fulltext_cn: 三星新闻中心
“银河之声”是一系列真实故事，聚焦于三星Galaxy用户如何将热情、创造力和决心与科技相结合，为自己的生活、社区和周围的世界带来积极影响。
对于37岁的急诊医生José Elías Ortega博士来说，他的智能手表曾经只是用来计步、管理通知和看时间。
但几年前，当他去探望独居的母亲时，他的Galaxy Watch帮助他做出了一项关键的决定。
一天早上，在医院值完夜班后，José Elías Ortega医生发现母亲躺在地板上，试图起身，但无法聚焦视线或回应他。凭借医学知识，他怀疑母亲中风了。然后他想起了自己的Galaxy Watch，并迅速将它戴在母亲的手腕上，以检查她的生命体征。
手表检测到她的血氧饱和度低于正常水平，这改变了José Elías Ortega医生的初步评估。他给她吸氧，并把她送往医院，医护团队诊断她患有流感性肺炎。幸运的是，他母亲的病情稳定下来，后来出院了。
“如果我当时没有佩戴这款手表……我们就不会意识到她有呼吸方面的问题，”José Elías Ortega医生说道。
Galaxy Watch改变了他的人生轨迹，而他母亲的获救只是一个开端。它还陪伴José Elías Ortega博士走过了他自己的甲状腺癌抗争之旅，帮助他改善了睡眠和活动习惯。
对于José Elías Ortega博士来说，这两次经历都表明了检测许多人容易忽视的健康信号的价值。来自可穿戴设备的数据并非要取代专业医疗服务，而是要告知用户潜在的健康问题，以便他们尽早寻求医疗护理。

cards.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
cards.title_cn: 科学家们在人工智能代理方面划定的界限
cards.summary: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
fulltext: 📄 Tech Report

Delegating research tasks to AI does not remove scientists’ responsibility for how the work is accomplished. For example, a researcher using AI to review the literature needs to check whether the system overlooks conflicting evidence or makes claims the cited papers don’t support. Someone handing off data analysis to an agentic system needs to understand which methods it used, which files it accessed, and whether the results can be successfully reproduced. A researcher automating part of a lab protocol needs confidence that the system respects physical safety constraints, such as temperature limits or material toxicity, while a researcher working with human-participant data needs assurance that a system protects participants' privacy and limits who can access their information. Researchers also need clear institutional guidelines for verifying and disclosing AI-assisted work.

These ethical and safety questions are central to our work on AI for science. Responsible science is about more than accuracy—scientific fields have ethical research norms because of past actions and choices by scientists and scientific communities, and those norms also cover how research is conducted and what impact it has. We want AI tools to expand what scientists can accomplish without compromising their ability to scrutinize evidence, verify methods, and – perhaps most importantly – stand behind their findings.

To better understand what that requires, we interviewed 17 scientists working in the natural, applied, and social sciences about the responsible development of AI agents. These systems can use tools and carry out research tasks with varying degrees of autonomy. The interviews drew on a network of researchers established through earlier survey work—we wanted to understand how scientists would steer AI’s development to reflect the responsibilities of their fields. We asked where researchers would welcome agentic assistance, what could go wrong, and what safeguards they would need to trust agents with their own studies.

Our interest in these questions grew out of work to evaluate the safety of models developed at Ai2. As we expand our focus on AI for science, we’ve found that much of the safety work on scientific applications emphasizes catastrophic risks in areas such as biology and nuclear physics. We also need ways to assess whether agents follow the standards of responsible conduct of research in the fields where they’re used.

One of our main findings concerns trust. Across the interviews, we identified five dimensions of scientific trust: validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability, and transparency. Together, they reflect concerns that go beyond whether an AI system produces a correct answer. Researchers also need to understand how an answer was reached, protect sensitive information, recognize bias, and determine who is charged with verifying and standing behind AI-assisted findings. These are matters of responsible conduct of research.

Another main finding suggests that scientists should help decide which research tasks agents take on, how those agents operate, and how their performance is evaluated. Even a technically correct result may be unsuitable for scientific use if researchers cannot inspect how it was produced, or if an agent accesses confidential data or files beyond what the researcher authorized.

A third key finding pertains to the future of science. Interviewees were divided between excitement about AI-driven progress and existential concern about the role of human scientists. They proposed training in AI use and named developing and enforcing guidelines as a critical, timely challenge.

For many participants in our interviews, the appeal of AI agents began with time-consuming research tasks—processing large datasets, writing code, documenting experimental procedures, and handling repetitive administrative work. Automating these activities could free researchers to spend more time on fieldwork, mentoring, or developing new ideas. It could also make it possible to analyze volumes of data that would be difficult to examine manually.
But delegating research tasks creates a corresponding need to verify the work an AI system performs.

Several participants described checking AI-generated answers against original publications rather than accepting summaries at face value. They worried about confident responses containing subtle inaccuracies, as well as tools that reinforce assumptions by retrieving only studies that support a favored hypothesis.

But checking the final answer from an AI system is only part of the challenge. Researchers may also need to know which sources an agent omitted, whether it followed the requested methodology, and what information it accessed along the way.

Our interviews suggest how evaluations of AI agents for scientific research could better reflect these concerns. A literature-review benchmark, for example, could test whether an agent overlooks contradictory evidence or draws conclusions unsupported by its sources. A coding benchmark could assess not only whether the generated code works, but whether the agent accesses files outside its authorized scope. Evaluations of data-processing agents could compare their methods and results with established human workflows.

These examples point toward a longer-term goal—a participatory benchmark in which scientists help define the research practices and safety requirements that agents should be tested against. We want to evaluate whether systems developed at Ai2 or elsewhere follow the standards of the fields where they’re used, as well as whether they complete assigned tasks.

These evaluations remain proposals to develop and test with scientists, rather than established solutions. But they offer a direction for our work at Ai2: building open scientific tools means making their behavior and limitations easier to investigate and giving the research community a role in defining what trustworthy performance looks like.

Verification is only one consideration in using AI tools for science. Respondents also raised a more fundamental question—what happens to scientific expertise when AI takes over parts of the research process?

An early-career biologist described deliberately limiting AI use while acquiring skills they hoped to teach future students. Another researcher questioned whether producing a correct result was sufficient if the researcher learned nothing in the process: even with perfect outputs, “did the person who obtained the perfect outputs get anything out of this?”

Some participants were concerned that AI-assisted research could diminish learning, though the value of automation depends in part on the researcher and the task. An experienced scientist may reasonably delegate a familiar procedure to save time, while someone still learning that procedure may benefit from doing the work themselves.

Participants also drew different boundaries around activities involving intellectual contribution. One biologist refused to use AI to generate research ideas, considering that a responsibility to retain personally. Others were more open to AI-assisted ideation or writing. An anthropologist, for example, argued that some sections of scientific papers, particularly routine descriptions of methods and results, are formulaic enough to benefit from automation.

Even researchers who tried AI for writing sometimes reconsidered. One political scientist described using Claude to help revise a manuscript, then deciding to rewrite the entire paper because the boundaries of their own intellectual contribution had become unclear. “I don’t know what was AI and what was me,” the researcher said.

Context mattered, too. Having AI critique a manuscript before submission was viewed favorably by some participants, while using it to review another researcher's unpublished work raised concerns. The distinction involves more than technical capability; peer review carries responsibilities around confidentiality, attribution, and the fair evaluation of others' research.

These disagreements suggest that responsible automation cannot be defined by a universal list of acceptable and unacceptable tasks. Scientific fields have different norms, and individual researchers may have different goals even when performing similar work.

The same tension applies to safeguards built into AI systems. One political scientist described how content restrictions that prevent AI tools from discussing certain topics could interfere with legitimate research on political violence or human rights violations. Meanwhile, participants working with sensitive human-subject data wanted stronger guarantees about privacy, access, and how information would be used.

Both are valid concerns. An agent that acts without sufficient safeguards could expose confidential data or produce harmful results, while one that’s constrained too broadly could prevent scientists from pursuing legitimate lines of inquiry.

This is why scientific communities need a meaningful role in shaping the boundaries of AI assistance. Developers need to understand not only which activities an agent can perform, but which decisions researchers want to retain and where safeguards are necessary—as well as where those safeguards might obstruct valuable work.
Our findings point toward an approach to scientific AI development that starts with the people who will use the technology.

Researchers should be able to examine an agent's contributions, determine which work to assign, and preserve opportunities to develop their own expertise. Achieving that will require technical features such as transparent records of agent actions and granular data controls, alongside evaluations informed by the standards and practices of different scientific communities.

It will also require continued collaboration. Our study is exploratory; the findings come from interviews with 17 US-based scientists, not a representative survey of scientific opinion or an empirical evaluation of specific AI agents. Participants discussed both the generative AI tools they use today and what they anticipate from more autonomous systems. Their perspectives identify important concerns and design priorities, rather than establishing a consensus about how AI should be used in science.

Still, they offer a path forward. At Ai2, we believe AI can accelerate scientific discovery while preserving the openness, reproducibility, and independent scrutiny that make research trustworthy. Through our broader efforts to develop and evaluate scientific agents, we aim to put those principles into practice. That means working with scientists to identify worthwhile uses for agents and translating their concerns into concrete evaluations, in addition to making it easier to understand both what these systems accomplish and how they accomplish it.

The promise of scientific AI isn't simply that researchers can pass off more work. It's that they can pursue questions that might otherwise be out of reach while retaining the knowledge, judgment, and agency needed to make discoveries that are their own.

cards.summary_cn: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】科学家们在人工智能代理方面划定的界限
fulltext_cn: 📄 技术报告

将研究任务委派给人工智能并不能免除科学家对工作完成方式的责任。例如，使用人工智能来查阅文献的研究人员需要检查系统是否忽视了相互矛盾的证据，或者是否提出了被引用的论文不支持的论断。将数据分析交给自主系统的人员需要了解该系统使用了哪些方法、访问了哪些文件，以及结果是否能够成功重现。将实验室规程的某一部分自动化的研究人员需要确信系统能够遵守物理安全限制，例如温度限制或材料毒性；而处理人类受试者数据的研究人员则需要确信系统能够保护受试者的隐私，并限制能够访问其信息的人员。研究人员还需要有明确的机构指南，用于核验和披露人工智能辅助的工作。
这些伦理和安全问题是我们开展“AI助力科学”工作的核心。负责任的科学不仅仅关乎准确性——由于科学家和科学界过去的行动和选择，科学领域存在着伦理研究规范，这些规范还涵盖了研究的开展方式及其影响。我们希望人工智能工具能够拓展科学家的能力边界，同时又不影响他们仔细审查证据、验证方法以及——也许最重要的是——坚持自己发现的能力。

为了更好地了解这需要什么，我们采访了17位从事自然科学、应用科学和社会科学工作的科学家，就负责任地开发人工智能体这一话题进行了探讨。这些系统可以使用工具，并以不同程度的自主性执行研究任务。这些访谈借鉴了通过早期调查工作建立的研究人员网络——我们希望了解科学家将如何引导人工智能的发展，以反映其所在领域的责任。我们询问了研究人员希望在哪些方面获得代理的协助、可能出现哪些问题，以及他们需要哪些保障措施才能放心地将自己的研究交给代理。
我们对这些问题的兴趣源于评估Ai2开发的模型安全性的工作。随着我们越来越多地关注用于科学的人工智能，我们发现，科学应用方面的许多安全工作都强调生物学和核物理学等领域的灾难性风险。我们还需要有方法来评估智能体是否在其应用领域遵守负责任研究行为的标准。
我们的主要发现之一与信任有关。在所有访谈中，我们确定了科学信任的五个维度：验证、隐私、客观性、问责制和透明度。这些方面加在一起，反映出人们的关切超出了人工智能系统是否给出正确答案的范畴。研究人员还需要了解得出答案的过程、保护敏感信息、识别偏见，并确定由谁负责核验人工智能辅助得出的结果并为其背书。这些是负责任地开展研究的问题。
另一项主要发现表明，科学家应协助决定代理应承担哪些研究任务、这些代理如何运作以及如何评估其表现。即使结果在技术上是正确的，如果研究人员无法检查其生成方式，或者如果代理访问了超出研究人员授权范围的机密数据或文件，那么该结果可能也不适合用于科学研究。
第三项关键发现与科学的未来有关。受访者对人工智能驱动的进步感到兴奋，但同时又对人类科学家的角色感到存在性担忧。他们建议开展人工智能使用方面的培训，并指出制定和实施准则是当前一项紧迫而关键的挑战。
对于我们访谈的许多参与者来说，AI代理的吸引力始于耗时的研究任务——处理大型数据集、编写代码、记录实验程序以及处理重复性行政工作。将这些活动自动化可以让研究人员腾出更多时间用于实地工作、指导或开拓新思路。它还可以使分析大量难以手动检查的数据成为可能。
但是，将研究任务委派出去，就相应地需要对人工智能系统所完成的工作进行核验。
多位参与者表示，他们会对照原始文献来核查人工智能生成的答案，而不是照单全收摘要内容。他们担心语气自信的回答中含有细微的错误，也担心工具只检索支持某一偏好假设的研究，从而强化了假设。
但是，检查人工智能系统的最终答案只是挑战的一部分。研究人员可能还需要了解代理省略了哪些来源、是否遵循了要求的方法，以及在此过程中访问了哪些信息。
我们的访谈表明，如何评估用于科学研究的AI代理才能更好地反映这些关切。例如，文献综述基准可以测试代理是否忽视了相互矛盾的证据，或者得出了其来源不支持的结论。编码基准不仅可以评估生成的代码是否有效，还可以评估代理是否访问了其授权范围之外的文件。对数据处理代理的评估可以将它们的方法和结果与既定的人工工作流程进行比较。
这些例子指向一个更长期的目标——一个参与式基准，其中科学家帮助确定应针对代理进行测试的研究实践和安全要求。我们希望评估在Ai2或其他地方开发的系统是否符合其使用领域的标准，以及是否能够完成指定的任务。
这些评估仍然是与科学家一起开发和测试的提案，而非既定解决方案。但它们为我们在Ai2的工作提供了方向：构建开放的科学工具意味着使人们更容易研究它们的行为和局限性，并让研究界在界定值得信赖的表现是什么方面发挥作用。
在将人工智能工具用于科学研究时，验证只是其中一个考虑因素。受访者还提出了一个更根本的问题——当人工智能接管部分研究过程时，科学专业知识会发生什么变化？
一位处于职业生涯初期的生物学家描述了自己在学习希望将来教给学生的技能时，故意限制人工智能的使用。另一位研究人员提出疑问，如果研究人员在过程中什么也没学到，那么得出正确的结果是否就足够了：即使得到了完美的结果，“获得完美结果的人从中得到了什么吗？”
一些参与者担心，人工智能辅助研究可能会削弱学习效果，但自动化的价值在一定程度上取决于研究人员和任务。经验丰富的科学家可能会合理地将熟悉的程序委托给他人，以节省时间，而仍在学习该程序的人则可能会从亲自动手做这项工作中受益。
参与者还对涉及智力贡献的活动划定了不同的界限。一位生物学家拒绝使用人工智能来生成研究想法，认为这是自己应承担的责任。其他人则更愿意接受人工智能辅助的构思或写作。例如，一位人类学家认为，科学论文的某些部分，特别是对方法和结果的常规描述，其模式化程度足以从自动化中受益。
即使是尝试过使用人工智能写作的研究人员，有时也会重新考虑。一位政治学学者描述了使用Claude来帮助修改一篇论文手稿的经历，然后他决定重写整篇论文，因为他自己的智力贡献的界限变得模糊不清。“我不知道哪些是人工智能的成果，哪些是我自己的成果，”该研究人员说道。
背景也很重要。一些参与者赞成在提交论文之前让人工智能对稿件进行评述，但使用人工智能来评审其他研究人员的未发表作品则引起了担忧。这种区别不仅仅涉及技术能力；同行评审还承担着保密、署名以及公正评价他人研究的责任。
这些分歧表明，负责任的自动化不能通过一份列出可接受和不可接受任务的通用清单来定义。科学领域有不同的规范，即使在从事类似工作时，个体研究人员也可能有着不同的目标。
同样的矛盾也适用于内置于人工智能系统中的保障措施。一位政治学家描述了阻止人工智能工具讨论某些话题的内容限制如何可能干扰对政治暴力或侵犯人权行为的合法研究。与此同时，处理敏感人类受试者数据的参与者希望在隐私、访问以及信息使用方式方面获得更有力的保障。
这两种担忧都有道理。如果没有足够的保障措施，代理的行动可能会泄露机密数据或产生有害结果；而如果限制过于宽泛，则可能会妨碍科学家开展合法的研究工作。
这就是为什么科学界需要在塑造人工智能辅助的边界方面发挥有意义的作用。开发人员不仅需要了解代理可以执行哪些活动，还需要了解研究人员希望保留哪些决策，以及哪些方面需要采取保障措施——以及这些保障措施可能在哪些方面妨碍有价值的工作。
我们的研究结果指向了一种科学的人工智能开发方法，这种方法从将使用该技术的人开始。
研究人员应能够审查代理的贡献，确定要分配哪些工作，并保留发展自身专业知识的机会。要实现这一点，需要具备透明记录代理行为和精细数据控制等技术功能，同时还需要根据不同科学界的标准和实践进行评估。
这也将需要持续的协作。我们的研究属于探索性研究；研究结果来自对17位美国科学家的访谈，而非对科学观点的具有代表性的调查，也不是对特定人工智能代理的实证评估。参与者讨论了他们目前使用的生成式人工智能工具，以及他们对更自主系统的期望。他们的观点旨在识别重要的关切事项和设计优先事项，而不是就人工智能在科学中的应用方式达成共识。
尽管如此，它们仍为我们指明了一条前进的道路。在Ai2，我们相信人工智能可以加速科学发现，同时又能保持开放性、可重复性和独立审查，从而使研究具有可信度。通过我们为开发和评估科学代理而开展的更广泛工作，我们旨在将这些原则付诸实践。这意味着要与科学家合作，确定代理的有价值用途，并将他们的关切转化为具体的评估，此外还要使人们更容易理解这些系统能实现什么以及如何实现。
科学人工智能的前景不仅仅在于研究人员可以转嫁更多的工作。而是他们可以探索原本可能遥不可及的问题，同时保留做出属于自己的发现所需的知识、判断力和自主性。

cards.title: Google Pixel Buds 2a drop 23% to match their lowest price
cards.title_cn: Google Pixel Buds 2a降价23%，创历史新低
cards.summary: 【Google】Google’s most affordable noise canceling earbuds are back at their best price. The Pixel Buds 2a are $99 on Amazon , which is $30 off the $129 list price, a 23% discount. That matches the lowest price…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Google’s most affordable noise canceling earbuds are back at their best price. The Pixel Buds 2a are $99 on Amazon, which is $30 off the $129 list price, a 23% discount. That matches the lowest price they’ve ever sold for, and every color is included.

You get active noise canceling and a Transparency mode, so you can block out a noisy commute or let the world back in with a tap. The earbuds run on Google’s Tensor A1 chip and weigh just 4.7g each, which makes them easy to wear for hours at a time.

Battery life is strong for earbuds at this price. You get up to seven hours from the buds with noise canceling on, or 10 hours with it off, and the case stretches that to 20 or 27 hours in total. The buds are IP54 rated against dust and splashes, and the case is IPX4, so a rainy walk or a sweaty workout is no problem.
They’re a natural match for Pixel phones, but the Pixel Buds 2a work with any Android phone or iPhone over Bluetooth. They also hold a 4.4-star rating on Amazon from more than 700 reviews.
This price has come around a few times this year, and it’s a good one to grab whether you want a pair for yourself or a gift for someone on your list this Black Friday season.

fulltext_cn: Android Authority上的联盟链接可能会为我们带来佣金。了解详情。
2026 年 11 月 25 日 — 美国东部时间中午 12:20
谷歌最实惠的降噪耳机又回到了最优惠的价格。Pixel Buds 2a在亚马逊上的售价为99美元，比129美元的标价便宜30美元，即享受7.7折优惠。这与它们有史以来的最低售价持平，且所有颜色均适用。
您可以使用主动降噪功能和通透模式，这样您就可以隔绝嘈杂的通勤环境，也可以轻触一下让外界声音重新传入。这款耳机采用谷歌的Tensor A1芯片，每只重量仅为4.7克，因此可以轻松佩戴数小时。
对于这个价位的耳机来说，电池续航能力很强。开启降噪功能时，耳机续航时间长达7小时，关闭降噪功能时，续航时间长达10小时，加上充电盒，总续航时间可延长至20小时或27小时。耳机具有IP54防尘防水溅等级，充电盒具有IPX4等级，因此在雨中散步或大汗淋漓地锻炼都没有问题。
它们与Pixel手机天生一对，但Pixel Buds 2a可以通过蓝牙与任何Android手机或iPhone配合使用。在亚马逊上，它们还获得了超过700条评价的4.4星评分。
今年这个价格已经出现过好几次了，无论您是想为自己买一双，还是想在今年的黑色星期五季为清单上的人买一双送礼，这都是一个不错的选择。
